newsitem.title: KENYA: Africa airlines warn safety problems could worsen.
newsitem.headline: Africa airlines warn safety problems could worsen.

text.p: African airlines conceded on Thursday there were shortcomings in airline safety on the continent and said the situation would only get worse because governments were failing to impose tough enough standards.
"With the increase in the number of private airlines that are being licensed by some African governments...the problem will be accentuated in future," the African Airlines Association (AFRAA) said.
It was responding to a report by the International Federation of Airline Pilots' Associations (IFALPA) on Wednesday which slammed the safety record of African airlines.
The report noted a marked increase in near-misses over Africa this year and said pilots rather than air traffic controllers were responsible for avoiding collisions.

"The operating conditions and inadequacies of the infrastructure are beyond argument (and) I feel the IFALPA statement dramatises the issue which has been known to Africa member airlines for some time," said senior AFRAA official Aberra Makonnen in the statement.

The African association blamed the problem on government failure to meet the minimum safety and operational standards required by established airlines in a statement that could diminish confidence in African air transport.

It recommended pilot training should take into account the continent's operating conditions, devices should be installed to avoid collisions and airport staff trained to remove obstacles from runways.
Nigerian authorities on Wednesday grounded a local airline whose Boeing 727 plane crashed two weeks ago killing all 142 on board.
Airline safety over most of Africa is appalling and a mid-air collision is just waiting to happen, IFALPA had said in its report.
